title: Martin Luther King Jr.
examples: What was the main goal of the Civil Rights Movement?
Can you tell me more about his speeches?
How did non-violence help the movement?

explain.say: Today we learn about Martin Luther King Jr. He was a very important leader.
The Civil Rights Movement fought for equal rights for African Americans. They wanted fairness for everyone.
His famous speech, I Have a Dream, was a powerful call for equality. It spoke of a better future for all people.
A key part of his message was non-violence. This meant protesting without using physical force or weapons.
In everyday life, we use non-violence when we disagree with someone. We can talk calmly instead of shouting.
A common mistake is thinking that speaking up means getting angry. Remember, strong words can be calm and powerful.

items: Speaking up means using your voice.
It does not mean shouting or getting angry.

faq.q: What was the main focus of the Civil Rights Movement?
faq.a: The movement aimed to end racial segregation and secure equal rights for African Americans in the United States.
asks: What did the Civil Rights Movement fight for?
Why was equality important during that time?

faq.q: What is the significance of the 'I Have a Dream' speech?
faq.a: It was a powerful speech that articulated the vision of a future where people were judged by their character, not their skin color.
asks: What message was in that famous speech?

faq.q: How did non-violence help the movement succeed?
faq.a: Non-violence allowed activists to maintain moral high ground, drawing attention to injustice without escalating the violence.
asks: What is the power of peaceful protest?

faq.q: Did Martin Luther King Jr. always agree with everyone?
faq.a: Like any leader, he faced disagreements, but his core message remained focused on justice and equality.

faq.q: Where did the Civil Rights Movement primarily take place?
faq.a: While it was a national movement, many key events and struggles took place in the American South.
asks: Where did the main protests happen?

facts: The movement fought against segregation, which kept groups of people separate.
Non-violence was a core philosophy taught by Martin Luther King Jr.
The 'I Have a Dream' speech was delivered in 1963.
The goal was to achieve full citizenship rights for all people.

quiz.say: The main goal of the Civil Rights Movement was to:

options.show: B) Equal rights for all citizens
options.say: B) Equal rights for all citizens

options.show: C) Moving to a new country
options.say: C) Moving to a new country

quiz.why: The movement's focus was on legal and social equality for all people.

wrong.1: This is too narrow; the fight was about more than just money.
wrong.2: The fight was to change laws where people already lived.
wrong.3: While leaders changed, the core fight was for rights, not just people in power.

quiz.say: If you are protesting injustice peacefully, you are using:
quiz.why: Non-violence means protesting without physical fighting or weapons.

wrong.0: Silence does not communicate the depth of the injustice you are facing.
wrong.1: Anger is a feeling, but non-violence is a disciplined action.
wrong.3: Using force escalates conflict and is not the peaceful method taught.

quiz.say: When Martin Luther King Jr. spoke of a 'dream', he was speaking about:

options.show: B) A vision of future equality
options.say: B) A vision of future equality

quiz.why: His 'dream' was a powerful public vision for a time when all people would be treated equally.

wrong.1: It was not just a private hope, but a public demand for change.
wrong.2: It was a vision for the future, not a description of the past.
wrong.3: It was deeper than a mere political promise; it was a moral vision.
